To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interpretation of the neutrino flux limits from stacked gamma-ray bursts depends on the underlying model assumptions.

spectral features in the neutrino flux are preserved in the diffuse flux limit, and that the flavor ratio is a powerful tool to constrain the Lorentz factor distribution of gamma-ray bursts, as well as their spectral shape.

spectral features are preserved in aggregated fluxes if only redshifts are considered, whereas they are smeared out in the Lorentz factor distribution, and the latter is model-dependent, which can be used as model discriminator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interpretation of neutrino flux limits from stacked and diffuse fluxes in the context of gamma-ray bursts.
the systematics in the interpretation of aggregated neutrino fluxes.
the systematics of aggregated flux limits and flavor ratios, and we show that the interpretation of such data requires caution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a significant detection of neutrinos from gamma-ray bursts will be the most convincing argument in favor of photohadronic interactions.
a neutrino flux limit in stacked samples, as well as in diffuse fluxes, does not allow to constrain the Lorentz factor of the source.
the neutrino flux from gamma-ray bursts is not suppressed at energies above 100 TeV, and that the flavor ratio is consistent with the standard flavor mixing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the interpretation of aggregated neutrino fluxes from gamma-ray bursts requires a careful consideration of the systematic effects introduced by the integration over the parameter distributions, and that the spectral features can be observed in aggregated neutrino flux limits, which would be an important step toward a better understanding of gamma-ray bursts.
, if the flavor ratio is used to discriminate between different models for the gamma-ray burst neutrino flux, the Lorentz factor distribution of the bursts should be considered as well.

, in the absence of a clear spectral signature, the flavor ratio is the only observable which can provide information on the source redshift distribution, whereas the neutrino flux is only sensitive to the Lorentz factor distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spectral features in stacked fluxes are not diluted, but are rather amplified by the low statistics of stacking samples, which is an important result for future analyses.
the interpretation of neutrino fluxes from stacked bursts is model dependent and requires a careful analysis of the underlying assumptions.
the interpretation of aggregated fluxes is more model dependent than that of single-burst analyses, and that it should be performed with care.
